findings.issue: Plaintext AWS credentials in EC2 user data
findings.risk: AWS_ACCESS_KEY_ID and AWS_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY are embedded in plaintext user data, which is retrievable by anyone with EC2 DescribeInstanceAttribute permissions or from within the instance via the metadata service, leading to full credential compromise
findings.remediation: Remove hardcoded credentials from user_data entirely. Assign an IAM instance profile (aws_iam_instance_profile) with least-privilege permissions to the instance and reference it via the iam_instance_profile attribute, allowing the instance to obtain temporary credentials via the metadata service

findings.risk: Without an instance profile the application has no managed identity, increasing the likelihood that developers embed long-lived static credentials (as seen in user_data) instead of using short-lived role credentials
findings.remediation: Create an aws_iam_role with a least-privilege policy, attach it to an aws_iam_instance_profile, and reference it in the aws_instance resource using the iam_instance_profile attribute

findings.risk: IMDSv1 allows unauthenticated HTTP requests to the metadata endpoint (169.254.169.254), making the instance vulnerable to SSRF-based credential theft. Any application-level SSRF can be used to steal IAM role credentials
findings.remediation: Add a metadata_options block to the aws_instance resource with http_tokens = "required" and http_endpoint = "enabled" to enforce IMDSv2

findings.risk: The root EBS volume is not encrypted, meaning data at rest on the OS disk (including logs, temp files, swap, and application data) is stored in plaintext and could be read if the volume is detached or a snapshot is taken
findings.remediation: Add a root_block_device block inside the aws_instance resource with encrypted = true and optionally specify a kms_key_id pointing to a customer-managed KMS key

findings.risk: Data written to the EBS volume is stored in plaintext. If the volume or a snapshot is accessed by an unauthorised party (e.g., via a misconfigured snapshot share or physical media reuse), the data is fully readable
findings.remediation: Set encrypted = true in the aws_ebs_volume resource and optionally specify kms_key_id with a customer-managed KMS CMK for additional key control

findings.issue: EBS snapshot created from an unencrypted volume
findings.risk: Because the source volume (aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage) is unencrypted, the resulting snapshot is also unencrypted. Unencrypted snapshots can be shared publicly or accessed by unauthorised accounts, exposing all data on the volume
findings.remediation: First encrypt the source volume (encrypted = true on aws_ebs_volume.web_host_storage). Alternatively, when creating the snapshot use the aws_ebs_snapshot_copy resource with encrypted = true and a kms_key_id to produce an encrypted copy

findings.issue: SSH port 22 open to the entire internet (0.0.0.0/0)
findings.risk: Exposing SSH to all IP addresses allows any actor on the internet to attempt brute-force or credential-stuffing attacks against the SSH service, significantly increasing the attack surface for unauthorised remote access
findings.remediation: Restrict the ingress rule for port 22 by replacing cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] with a specific trusted CIDR range (e.g., your corporate NAT gateway IP). Prefer using AWS Systems Manager Session Manager and remove the SSH ingress rule entirely

findings.issue: Unrestricted outbound egress (0.0.0.0/0 on all ports)
findings.risk: Allowing all outbound traffic means a compromised instance can freely exfiltrate data, download malware, communicate with command-and-control servers, or pivot to other services without any network-level control
findings.remediation: Replace the catch-all egress rule with specific rules that permit only the required outbound destinations and ports (e.g., port 443 to specific service endpoints). Remove or tightly scope the protocol = "-1" / cidr_blocks = ["0.0.0.0/0"] egress rule

findings.issue: Public IP automatically assigned to instances in subnet
findings.risk: map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched in this subnet receives a public IP address, directly exposing it to the internet and increasing the attack surface unnecessarily
findings.remediation: Set map_public_ip_on_launch = false. Place instances in a private subnet and use a NAT gateway for outbound internet access. Expose services externally only through a load balancer in a dedicated public subnet

findings.issue: Public IP automatically assigned to instances in subnet
findings.risk: map_public_ip_on_launch = true means every instance launched in this subnet receives a public IP address, directly exposing it to the internet and increasing the attack surface unnecessarily
findings.remediation: Set map_public_ip_on_launch = false. Place instances in a private subnet and use a NAT gateway for outbound internet access. Expose services externally only through a load balancer in a dedicated public subnet

findings.issue: Missing S3 Block Public Access configuration
findings.risk: Without an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource, the bucket could be made public via a bucket policy or ACL change, potentially exposing VPC flow log data (IP addresses, ports, traffic patterns) to the public internet
findings.remediation: Add an aws_s3_bucket_public_access_block resource referencing this bucket with block_public_acls = true, block_public_policy = true, ignore_public_acls = true, and restrict_public_buckets = true

findings.issue: S3 bucket server-side encryption not enabled
findings.risk: Flow log data stored in the bucket is not encrypted at rest. If bucket permissions are misconfigured or the bucket is accessed by an unauthorised party, network traffic metadata is readable in plaintext
findings.remediation: Add an aws_s3_bucket_server_side_encryption_configuration resource for this bucket specifying AES256 or aws:kms encryption via the apply_server_side_encryption_by_default block

findings.risk: Without versioning, flow log objects can be overwritten or deleted (accidentally or maliciously) with no ability to recover previous versions, undermining the integrity and availability of audit/forensic data
findings.remediation: Add an aws_s3_bucket_versioning resource for this bucket with versioning_configuration { status = "Enabled" }

findings.issue: S3 bucket access logging not enabled
findings.risk: Without server access logging on the flow-log bucket itself, there is no audit trail of who accessed or modified the bucket, making it impossible to detect unauthorised access to sensitive network flow data
findings.remediation: Add an aws_s3_bucket_logging resource targeting a separate dedicated logging bucket to capture all access requests to the flowbucket

findings.issue: VPC Flow Logs capture only to S3 without log file validation or encryption in transit enforcement
findings.risk: Flow logs delivered to S3 without enforcing TLS (via a bucket policy requiring aws:SecureTransport) can be intercepted in transit. Additionally, without integrity validation it is impossible to detect if log files have been tampered with
findings.remediation: Attach an aws_s3_bucket_policy to aws_s3_bucket.flowbucket that denies any request where aws:SecureTransport is false. Also enable SSE-KMS on the bucket so logs are encrypted at rest with a CMK that has its own key policy and rotation enabled
